clue.text: Mantra thought cynical provokes new high street riot: police only at the end sent in

indicators.note: something sent in is inserted, so the single letter goes into the mixed letters
to provoke is to stir up, so these words are stirred into a new order
only the end of the word police is wanted, its final letter

explanation.surface: A news report of a high street disturbance that police reached only late, with a cynical slogan to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provokes' rearranges NEW HIGH STREET RIOT; 'sent in' adds E, the last letter of 'police', among those letters. The slogan was George Osborne's 2009 call for shared austerity.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase was a Conservative austerity slogan, widely seen as a hollow mantra of shared sacrifice.

clue.text: Self-interested people say it's so messed up

parts.note: say introduces an example, abbreviated e.g.

indicators.note: messed up means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that something is in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' as 'for example' gives its abbreviation; the apostrophe in 'it's' is ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Egotistical people put their own interests first, which is what self-interested means.

clue.text: Given relief since being trapped in rising river

indicators.note: being trapped in puts one piece inside another
in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the river's name is reversed

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
since and as both mean because

explanation.surface: Someone was rescued after being stuck in a swelling river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses the river (a down clue reads upward), and 'being trapped in' sets the second piece inside: E-AS-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease pain or worry is to relieve it, so eased matches given relief as a past participle.

clue.text: Newspaper for citizen

definitions.meaning: a citizen of a country is one of its ...

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a Scottish daily paper and a person belonging to a particular nation.

clue.text: Writer and Pharaoh to supply some ups and downs here?

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, flexibly bent, so these words are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A writer and an Egyptian king provide some highs and lows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is read as 'in a supple way', rearranging WRITER, PHARAOH and TO. The 'ups and downs' are planes taking off and landing.
explanation.definitionFit: London's main airport sees constant take-offs and landings, the ups and downs of flights.

clue.text: Our compiler-cum-detective

definitions.meaning: A pseudonym of a Financial Times crossword setter
a detective is an investigator or private eye

explanation.definitionFit: The word is the pen name of a Financial Times setter and also an everyday word for an investigator.

clue.text: Party for Winnie on Radio Antelope?

indicators.note: something heard on the radio is only heard, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: Winnie the Pooh's party would be a Pooh do

explanation.surface: A celebration for a bear, broadcast on the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on Radio' says POOH DO aloud. The pudu is a tiny South American deer, not an antelope, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A pudu is a very small deer, a hoofed grazer loosely like an antelope, as the question mark admits.

clue.text: Penny Coolidge corrupted one taking lead in war on crime

definitions.text: one taking lead in war on crime

indicators.note: corrupted means spoiled or altered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former US president paid off in pennies, joining the fight against crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupted' rearranges COOLIDGE (US president Calvin Coolidge) after P.
explanation.definitionFit: A police dog is led on a lead by its handler while it works against criminals.

Ecologically conscious folk on move — or those in 5 queues!

definitions.meaning: New Age itinerants living close to nature in vans and buses
people waiting in line at the airport to fly

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both roving New Age itinerants and anyone making a journey, such as passengers at an airport.

clue.text: Taken over by American news boss, holy publication did

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

indicators.note: taken over means turned over, so the scripture abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A sacred journal was bought by an American media mogul.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken over' reverses OT, the Old Testament, to TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Habitual past action: 'I did go there often' and 'I used to go there' say the same thing.

clue.text: Essential thing wily caliph grasps is to reach good speed

indicators.note: grasps means holds, so one piece goes inside the other
wily means crafty, hinting the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: it, as in 'that's it', is the essential thing

explanation.surface: A cunning ruler seizes what really matters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wily' rearranges the caliph to HACLIP, and 'grasps' holds the essential thing within. To hit a clip is everyday speech for going fast.
explanation.definitionFit: To go at a fast clip is to move briskly, so hitting one is reaching a good pace.

clue.text: Very large girl as compared with figure seen in bars

parts.note: OS stands for outsize
Tina is a girl's name
to as in 'ten to one', a comparison

explanation.surface: A big girl is set against someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bars' are musical bars, not pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, an ostinato is a short phrase repeated persistently through many bars.

clue.text: Homes around castle grand as appropriate

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the homes go round the castle

parts.note: IN means at home, and two of them are homes
a keep is a castle's main tower
G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Houses built round a fortress, as suits it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homes' is two lots of 'at home'; 'around' makes them wrap the castle tower, one on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in keeping is consistent with its setting, suitable or fitting.

clue.text: Money to chime with 26 perhaps unsurprisingly?

definitions.text: Money to chime with 26 perhaps unsurprisingly?

parts.words: Money to chime with 26 perhaps unsurprisingly?
parts.note: slang for cash that rhymes with the upper-class word at 26, as rich people would be

explanation.definitionFit: British slang for cash, which also rhymes with the word meaning upper-class.

clue.text: Good coin and currency reduced in splendour

parts.note: the rand is the South African currency and coin

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter of the currency goes

parts.note: the euro is the European currency

explanation.surface: Fine money and cash cut back in grand circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts EURO to EUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur and splendour are synonyms for impressive magnificence.

clue.text: Cost of this unknown to leader in monied class?

indicators.note: the leader in a word is its opening letter

parts.note: ilk means kind or class

explanation.surface: A rich ruling-class politician has no idea what everyday things cost.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the theme: posh politicians were mocked for not knowing the price of a pint of milk.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue describes a staple whose price posh politicians were mocked for not knowing.

clue.text: Principal from Islington gets on very slowly in divorce

indicators.note: the principal letter of a word is its first

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so good'
late means behind time, slow to arrive

explanation.surface: A head teacher from a London borough is making slow progress through a split.
explanation.walkthrough: Islington is a borough of north London. 'divorce' is a verb here: to cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: To divorce one thing from another is to separate or cut it off, as isolating does.

clue.text: Causing uproar in HP, Tory's central pair, as snooty, brag?

definitions.text: Causing uproar in HP, Tory's central pair, as snooty, brag?

indicators.note: an uproar throws things into disorder, so the letters that follow are jumbled
the central pair of letters of Tory are its two middle ones

explanation.surface: A question whether boasting, snooty Tory types are behaving outrageously in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Causing uproar in' rearranges HP, OR (the middle of 'Tory'), AS, SNOOTY and BRAG. HP is hire purchase, buying on instalments. The phrase was Nadine Dorries's 2012 jibe at Cameron and Osborne.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue paints snobbish boasting Tories, which is exactly the insult Dorries aimed at her party's leaders.

clue.text: Geek for the most part accepts task, but employer he isn't!

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the task goes inside
most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: a geek is a nerd
an onus is a burden or duty

explanation.surface: A computer geek takes on a job, but is not the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops the geek's last letter, and 'accepts' takes the task in. An employer here is one who employs something, a user.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is one who employs something, so someone who isn't one makes no use of it.

clue.text: Husband in short cloak left union group

indicators.note: in places the husband inside the cloak

parts.note: a cape is a short cloak

explanation.surface: A husband wrapped in a little cloak walks out on a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: In British printing and journalism unions a branch at a workplace is called a chapel.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapel is a branch of a printers' or journalists' trade union at one workplace.

clue.text: See 1
Love is confused with inner dread for Tory denouncing 19 26 9

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Love gets muddled with a deep-seated fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges O (love, a zero score in tennis), IS, INNER and DREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the Conservative MP who called Cameron and Osborne the snobbish insult the cross-reference spells out.

clue.text: Best boy makes stand in warehouse

indicators.note: in a down clue standing up means reading from the bottom, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: top means best
Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A movie's best boy builds a stand in a storage shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes stand' turns TOPED upright, reading DEPOT. A best boy is also a film crew job.
explanation.definitionFit: A depot is a storehouse for goods, the same as a warehouse.

clue.text: With device for mobile chat, page husband in BBC station

indicators.note: in places the two letters inside the station's name

parts.note: Radio One is a BBC pop music station

explanation.surface: Someone pages a husband who works at a BBC station using a phone.
explanation.walkthrough: Radio One is the BBC's pop music station.
explanation.definitionFit: A radiophone sends speech by radio waves, letting people talk while on the move.

clue.text: See 19
He composed letter after a certain amount of work

parts.note: the letter after A in the alphabet is B
an erg is a unit of work in physics

explanation.surface: Someone wrote a letter once a set amount of work was done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after a' is not a placing signal: the letter after A is B. Alban Berg was an Austrian composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Alban Berg was an Austrian composer of the Second Viennese School.

clue.text: Work by Spenser for instance illuminated times by river

parts.note: lit means illuminated
an era is a period of time
T is short for time
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A poet's writing read by lamplight, from a riverside era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'times' gives two times, ERA and T. Edmund Spenser wrote The Faerie Queene.
explanation.definitionFit: Spenser's poetry is classic English writing, an example of the body of written work.
